How to read this report
  • A run's score is the weighted fraction of its graders that passed; a "perfect" run passed every grader.
  • A case's score is the mean of its runs; a case passes when its score is at or above the 100% threshold (the tick on each case bar).
  • The suite score is the mean of the per-case scores.
  • Judge votes are independent samples of the LLM judge; the majority decides pass or fail.
  • No baseline arm was run (ablation off) — this report shows absolute scores only and cannot say whether the plugin caused them. Re-run with --ablation with-without to measure the plugin’s effect.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
I found most of these through secondary sources. NCBI's GEO and dbGaP pages blocked my fetches with a browser check, so I couldn't open the GEO records myself. Accessions marked "from memory" were not confirmed by any search result.

## Download now (open access)

| Cohort | Drug and cancer | Where | Verified? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hugo 2016** | anti-PD-1, melanoma, about 28 patients | GEO [GSE78220](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE78220) | Accession confirmed by a paper. Page not opened. |
| **Riaz 2017** | nivolumab, melanoma, pre- and on-treatment biopsies | GEO [GSE91061](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE91061) (also SRP094781, PRJNA356761) | Accession confirmed by a paper. Page not opened. |
| **Gide 2019** | anti-PD-1 with or without anti-CTLA-4, melanoma | Raw reads from ENA PRJEB23709. Clinical data from the paper. | Confirmed by papers. Processed data is also on TIGER. |
| **Kim 2018** | pembrolizumab, gastric cancer, 61 patients | ENA [PRJEB25780](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/PRJEB25780) | The BioProject exists. I couldn't confirm that it holds the RNA-seq, so check the ENA record. |
| **IMvigor210** (Mariathasan 2018) | atezolizumab, urothelial, 348 patients | Processed counts and clinical data in the [IMvigor210CoreBiologies tarball](http://research-pub.gene.com/IMvigor210CoreBiologies/IMvigor210CoreBiologies.tar.gz) under CC 3.0. Raw data is on EGA. | Confirmed. About 298 patients have response data. |
| **Braun 2020** | nivolumab, ccRCC (CheckMate 009, 010 and 025) | Normalised RNA-seq, clinical and mutation data in the Nature Medicine supplementary file `41591_2020_839_MOESM2_ESM.xlsx` | Confirmed by papers. Raw data is on EGA (see below). |

Notes on these cohorts:
- **IMvigor210 package:** it needs the old DESeq package, which is no longer on Bioconductor. One reanalysis reads the saved data objects from the tarball directly with only Biobase.
- **Riaz and Hugo response labels:** I didn't check how response is coded in these. RECIST categories and the pre-treatment versus on-treatment labels in Riaz need care so that on-treatment samples don't leak into training.

## Apply for access

- **Raw IMvigor210:** EGA [EGAS00001002556](https://ega-archive.org/studies/EGAS00001002556), controlled access. You probably don't need it, because the processed counts are already open.
- **IMvigor210/211/130/010 combined (Cancer Cell 2024):** EGA EGAS50000000497, which I did not open.
- **IMmotion150 and PCD4989g (renal and other):** EGA EGAS00001004343, restricted.
- **Braun raw data:** a Cancer Cell paper cites EGA EGAS00001004290, EGAS00001004291 and EGAS00001004292. Braun's own data statement may differ, so check it.
- **Liu 2019 (melanoma, anti-PD-1):** dbGaP phs000452.v3.p1, according to one paper. The same paper says the data is also on cBioPortal, which may be the quicker route.
- **Miao 2018 (ccRCC, CheckMate 009):** dbGaP phs001493, taken from a Cancer Cell paper that sourced its raw RNA-seq there.
- **MGH melanoma:** dbGaP phs002683.v1.p1, according to one paper. GEO GSE115821 and GSE168204 are also listed as MGH cohorts. I didn't check their access status, so confirm whether they are open.

## Other candidates

- **Amato:** GEO GSE145996, melanoma anti-PD-1, 52 patients with WES and RNA-seq. This was only listed in a search result.
- **Van Allen 2015:** an anti-CTLA-4 melanoma cohort used as validation in several papers. Its dbGaP accession is phs000452 from memory, which matches Liu's accession, so verify it.
- **GSE120575:** this is single-cell data, so it isn't suitable for a bulk classifier.

## Suggestions

1. **Start with the open cohorts.** Hugo, Riaz, Gide, IMvigor210, Kim and Braun cover melanoma, urothelial, gastric and renal cancer, and use anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1 and anti-CTLA-4.
2. **Check for overlap.** Several melanoma cohorts share patients or pre-treatment samples across papers, which would inflate cross-study validation.
3. **Harmonise the platforms.** The cohorts mix FPKM, TPM and raw counts, so reprocess or rank-normalise them consistently.
4. **Verify GEO details in a browser.** Check the sample counts and the response columns before you commit to a design.

I can run the ENA and GEO checks through their APIs if you'd like. They may be reachable from here even though the NCBI web pages were blocked.

Sources:
- [Melanoma cohort accession search results](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12410410/)
- [Nature Communications, molecular patterns of resistance in melanoma](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-47425-y)
- [Cancer Cell 2024, urothelial carcinoma](https://www.cell.com/cancer-cell/fulltext/S1535-6108(24)00404-5?uuid=uuid%3A3f29ac99-d89a-46ff-ad73-5698e4fb578e)
- [Kim 2018 in Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-018-0101-z)
- [PRJEB25780 on BioProject](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/PRJEB25780)
- [PRJEB40416 on BioProject](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/PRJEB40416)
- [Cancer Cell 2021, tumor and immune reprogramming in renal cell carcinoma](https://www.cell.com/cancer-cell/fulltext/S1535-6108(21)00117-3)
- [Nature Communications, 9p21 loss](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-25894-9)
- [PMC9382843, IO score in urothelial cancer](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9382843/)

Several accessions are verified against the registry records and some rest on secondary sources. I've marked which is which. NCBI's GEO web pages blocked my fetches with a CAPTCHA, so I confirmed the GEO records through NCBI's E-utilities API instead.

## Download now (open access)

| Cohort | Cancer / treatment | n (RNA-seq) | Where | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Hugo 2016** | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 | 28 | [GSE78220](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE78220) | Record confirmed via E-utilities (pre-treatment biopsies, RNA-seq) |
| **Riaz 2017** | Melanoma, nivolumab, with pre- and on-treatment samples | 109 samples | [GSE91061](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE91061) | Record confirmed via E-utilities |
| **Gide 2019** | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-1 + anti-CTLA-4 | not checked | ENA [PRJEB23709](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/api/xml/PRJEB23709) | Status PUBLIC, RNA-seq. Fetched directly. |
| **Amato 2020** | Melanoma, anti-PD-1, RECIST 1.1 | see caveat | [GSE145996](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE145996) | Record exists. The summary says 52 patients, but the record lists only 14 samples. Check the files before relying on it. |
| **Mariathasan 2018 (IMvigor210)** | Urothelial, atezolizumab | 348 | [IMvigor210CoreBiologies R package](http://research-pub.gene.com/IMvigor210CoreBiologies/) (CC 3.0 licence) | Found via search, not downloaded. It contains processed counts and clinical data, and it's the easiest large cohort to get. |
| **Braun 2020** | Clear-cell RCC, nivolumab (CheckMate 009/010/025) | about 311 combined | Supplementary tables of [the Nature Medicine paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-020-0839-y) | A reuse paper reports normalized expression and clinical data in the supplement. I didn't open the paper myself. |
| **Kim 2018** | Gastric, pembrolizumab | about 45–61 | ENA [PRJEB25780](https://www.omicsdi.org/dataset/project/PRJEB25780). Processed versions are on [CRI iAtlas](https://cri-iatlas.org/resources/) and TIDE. | Project listing confirmed. Reports of the usable n differ between papers. |

[CRI iAtlas](https://cri-iatlas.org/about/) harmonizes about 23 immuno-oncology datasets, including Riaz, Miao, Kim, Anders (TNBC, pembrolizumab), Padrón (pancreatic) and Rose (urothelial). It's worth checking for ready-made matrices, but verify each study's access terms there.

GSE168204 (27 samples) is not a new cohort. It's a pathway-signature paper that reuses the Riaz, Hugo and other data, so don't count it as an independent validation set.

## Apply for access (controlled)

- **Mariathasan raw data:** EGA [EGAS00001002556](https://ega-archive.org/studies/EGAS00001002556), with RNA-seq dataset EGAD00001003977 (348 samples). You'd only need this if you want to re-process from raw reads. The EGA page didn't state the DAC, so check the dataset page.
- **Liu 2019 and Van Allen 2015 (melanoma):** dbGaP [phs000452](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12410410/). Sources disagree on whether v2 or v3 maps to which study, so check the version when you apply.
- **Miao 2018 (RCC):** dbGaP phs001493.
- **Ravi 2023 (NSCLC, SU2C-MARK):** dbGaP [phs002822.v1.p1](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-023-01355-5), which has about 393 patients with WES and/or RNA-seq. It has site-specific use restrictions, including disease-specific use. It is the largest lung cohort I found.
- **Newer MGH melanoma cohort:** dbGaP phs002683.v1.p1.
- **Braun 2020 raw data:** EGA EGAS00001004290, EGAS00001004291 and EGAS00001004292. These came from a secondary citation, so confirm them.
- **McDermott 2018 (RCC, atezolizumab):** EGA EGAS00001002928.

## Not verified
- I found no data-access information for Cho (NSCLC).
- I didn't find or check the full Ravi accession list beyond the two above.
- I didn't verify the n for Gide or any response-label coding, so you'll need to check each cohort's clinical table.

## Practical advice
- **Starting set:** Hugo, Riaz, Gide and Amato (melanoma), plus IMvigor210 (bladder), Braun (RCC) and Kim (gastric). That gives you about seven cohorts across four cancer types with no applications.
- **Batch effects:** Cohorts differ in platform, tissue handling and treatment line. Plan for cross-study normalization.
- **Response labels:** Riaz includes on-treatment samples, so filter to pre-treatment. Labels are mixed between RECIST and clinical benefit, so harmonize them.
- **Overlap:** The Gide and Riaz cohorts might include some of the same patients as other cohorts, so check for duplicates.

Several accessions are verified against the registry records and some rest on secondary sources. I've marked which is which. NCBI's GEO web pages blocked my fetches with a CAPTCHA, so I confirmed the GEO records through NCBI's E-utilities API instead.

## Download now (open access)

| Cohort | Cancer / treatment | n (RNA-seq) | Where | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Hugo 2016** | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 | 28 | [GSE78220](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE78220) | Record confirmed via E-utilities (pre-treatment biopsies, RNA-seq) |
| **Riaz 2017** | Melanoma, nivolumab, with pre- and on-treatment samples | 109 samples | [GSE91061](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE91061) | Record confirmed via E-utilities |
| **Gide 2019** | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-1 + anti-CTLA-4 | not checked | ENA [PRJEB23709](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/api/xml/PRJEB23709) | Status PUBLIC, RNA-seq. Fetched directly. |
| **Amato 2020** | Melanoma, anti-PD-1, RECIST 1.1 | see caveat | [GSE145996](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE145996) | Record exists. The summary says 52 patients, but the record lists only 14 samples. Check the files before relying on it. |
| **Mariathasan 2018 (IMvigor210)** | Urothelial, atezolizumab | 348 | [IMvigor210CoreBiologies R package](http://research-pub.gene.com/IMvigor210CoreBiologies/) (CC 3.0 licence) | Found via search, not downloaded. It contains processed counts and clinical data, and it's the easiest large cohort to get. |
| **Braun 2020** | Clear-cell RCC, nivolumab (CheckMate 009/010/025) | about 311 combined | Supplementary tables of [the Nature Medicine paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-020-0839-y) | A reuse paper reports normalized expression and clinical data in the supplement. I didn't open the paper myself. |
| **Kim 2018** | Gastric, pembrolizumab | about 45–61 | ENA [PRJEB25780](https://www.omicsdi.org/dataset/project/PRJEB25780). Processed versions are on [CRI iAtlas](https://cri-iatlas.org/resources/) and TIDE. | Project listing confirmed. Reports of the usable n differ between papers. |

[CRI iAtlas](https://cri-iatlas.org/about/) harmonizes about 23 immuno-oncology datasets, including Riaz, Miao, Kim, Anders (TNBC, pembrolizumab), Padrón (pancreatic) and Rose (urothelial). It's worth checking for ready-made matrices, but verify each study's access terms there.

GSE168204 (27 samples) is not a new cohort. It's a pathway-signature paper that reuses the Riaz, Hugo and other data, so don't count it as an independent validation set.

## Apply for access (controlled)

- **Mariathasan raw data:** EGA [EGAS00001002556](https://ega-archive.org/studies/EGAS00001002556), with RNA-seq dataset EGAD00001003977 (348 samples). You'd only need this if you want to re-process from raw reads. The EGA page didn't state the DAC, so check the dataset page.
- **Liu 2019 and Van Allen 2015 (melanoma):** dbGaP [phs000452](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12410410/). Sources disagree on whether v2 or v3 maps to which study, so check the version when you apply.
- **Miao 2018 (RCC):** dbGaP phs001493.
- **Ravi 2023 (NSCLC, SU2C-MARK):** dbGaP [phs002822.v1.p1](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-023-01355-5), which has about 393 patients with WES and/or RNA-seq. It has site-specific use restrictions, including disease-specific use. It is the largest lung cohort I found.
- **Newer MGH melanoma cohort:** dbGaP phs002683.v1.p1.
- **Braun 2020 raw data:** EGA EGAS00001004290, EGAS00001004291 and EGAS00001004292. These came from a secondary citation, so confirm them.
- **McDermott 2018 (RCC, atezolizumab):** EGA EGAS00001002928.

## Not verified
- I found no data-access information for Cho (NSCLC).
- I didn't find or check the full Ravi accession list beyond the two above.
- I didn't verify the n for Gide or any response-label coding, so you'll need to check each cohort's clinical table.

## Practical advice
- **Starting set:** Hugo, Riaz, Gide and Amato (melanoma), plus IMvigor210 (bladder), Braun (RCC) and Kim (gastric). That gives you about seven cohorts across four cancer types with no applications.
- **Batch effects:** Cohorts differ in platform, tissue handling and treatment line. Plan for cross-study normalization.
- **Response labels:** Riaz includes on-treatment samples, so filter to pre-treatment. Labels are mixed between RECIST and clinical benefit, so harmonize them.
- **Overlap:** The Gide and Riaz cohorts might include some of the same patients as other cohorts, so check for duplicates.

I found sources for all of these through web search, but I could only partly verify them. NCBI's GEO pages returned a bot-check page, and the Genentech host refused my connection. So the accessions and access routes below come from search results and papers that cite them. I did not open the repository records. Check each record before you build on it.

## Download now (no application)

| Cohort | Cancer / drug | Accession | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hugo 2016 | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 | GEO GSE78220 | 28 patients with pre-treatment RNA-seq |
| Riaz 2017 | Melanoma, nivolumab | GEO GSE91061 (also SRP094781, PRJNA356761) | 68 patients, 108 biopsies. Includes both pre-treatment and on-treatment samples, so filter to pre-treatment. Some patients had prior anti-CTLA-4. |
| Gide 2019 | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 alone or with anti-CTLA-4 | ENA PRJEB23709 | Not in GEO. One paper lists EGA EGAD00001005738, so check whether the raw data are open or controlled. |
| Amato | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 | GEO GSE145996 | 52 patients with exome and RNA-seq. I haven't checked how response is annotated. |
| Jung 2019 | NSCLC, anti-PD-1/PD-L1 | GEO GSE135222 | Only 27 patients (7 durable clinical benefit, 20 non-benefit, using PFS > 180 days). |
| Kim 2018 | Gastric, pembrolizumab | ENA ERP107734 | 61 patients deposited. Downstream papers used only 39–45 because of problems with the expression matrix. |
| IMvigor210 | Urothelial, atezolizumab | R package `IMvigor210CoreBiologies` from research-pub.gene.com/IMvigor210CoreBiologies/ | Processed counts and clinical data, including RECIST response. Papers cite 298 to 348 patients. Raw reads are controlled-access (see below). |

## Needs an application, or has restricted raw data

- **Liu 2019 (melanoma, anti-PD-1):** dbGaP phs000452.v3.p1. One paper says it can also be downloaded from cBioPortal, which would let you skip dbGaP for processed data.
- **Van Allen 2015 (melanoma, anti-CTLA-4):** this is the anti-CTLA-4 cohort you'd want, but I did not confirm its accession. I believe it is also under dbGaP phs000452, so verify that.
- **Miao 2018 (ccRCC):** dbGaP phs001493, controlled access.
- **Mariathasan 2018 (IMvigor210 raw data):** EGA EGAS00001002556, controlled access. The processed package above is enough for most uses.
- **Braun 2020 (nivolumab, ccRCC, CheckMate 025):** EGA EGAS00001004290, EGAS00001004291 and EGAS00001004292. EGA requires a Data Access Committee request. One citing paper describes the deposited data as normalized RNA-seq rather than raw. That description is second-hand.
- **MGH melanoma cohort:** dbGaP phs002683.v1.p1.

## Shortcuts: curated compendia

- **TIDE** (tide.dfci.harvard.edu) hosts processed data from published ICB trials. One comparison table counts about 1,247 patients.
- **CRI iAtlas** has preprocessed expression data in TPM, plus clinical and treatment information. A 2026 preprint downloaded 8 cohorts from it.
- **ICBatlas** (bioinfo.life.hust.edu.cn/ICBatlas/) covers 1,515 samples from 25 studies across nine cancer types. I couldn't confirm that it offers bulk download.
- **Cancer-Immu and ICB-Portal** are compared in the bioRxiv review linked below. Cancer-Immu lists 3,652 patients.

## Practical notes

- **Open-access starting set:** Hugo, Riaz, Gide, Amato, IMvigor210, Kim and Jung. That is four melanoma cohorts plus bladder, gastric and lung. Add Liu and Van Allen (via dbGaP or cBioPortal) for more melanoma, and Braun or Miao for kidney.
- **Pre-treatment samples:** Riaz includes on-treatment biopsies and the MGH GSE115821/GSE168204 cohorts include both timepoints. Keep only pre-treatment samples to avoid leakage.
- **Response definitions:** these differ between cohorts (RECIST, durable clinical benefit by PFS, and so on). Harmonize them before pooling.
- **Batch effects:** the cohorts were run on different platforms and pipelines. Plan to reprocess raw data or use cross-cohort normalization, and validate leave-one-cohort-out.
- **Overlap:** check for patients appearing in more than one cohort before you split train and test sets.
- **Not for your use case:** GSE120575 is single-cell, not bulk.

Sources:
- [Search: melanoma anti-PD-1 RNA-seq cohort accessions](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13687651)
- [Combined tumor and immune signals… (Cell Reports Medicine)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666379121003773)
- [Review of ICB transcriptome databases (bioRxiv)](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.12.09.627506v1.full)
- [Large-scale public data reuse to model immunotherapy response (TIDE)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7045518/)
- [ICBatlas (Cancer Immunology Research)](https://aacrjournals.org/cancerimmunolres/article/10/11/1398/709876/ICBatlas-A-Comprehensive-Resource-for-Depicting)
- [A Pan-Cancer Immunogenomic Atlas for ICB](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9189237/)
- [IMvigor210 ML paper (npj Precision Oncology)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41698-025-00969-8)
- [Tumor and immune reprogramming in RCC (Cancer Cell)](https://www.cell.com/cancer-cell/fulltext/S1535-6108(21)00117-3)
- [Kim 2018 gastric (PubMed)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30013197/)

I found sources for all of these through web search, but I could only partly verify them. NCBI's GEO pages returned a bot-check page, and the Genentech host refused my connection. So the accessions and access routes below come from search results and papers that cite them. I did not open the repository records. Check each record before you build on it.

## Download now (no application)

| Cohort | Cancer / drug | Accession | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hugo 2016 | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 | GEO GSE78220 | 28 patients with pre-treatment RNA-seq |
| Riaz 2017 | Melanoma, nivolumab | GEO GSE91061 (also SRP094781, PRJNA356761) | 68 patients, 108 biopsies. Includes both pre-treatment and on-treatment samples, so filter to pre-treatment. Some patients had prior anti-CTLA-4. |
| Gide 2019 | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 alone or with anti-CTLA-4 | ENA PRJEB23709 | Not in GEO. One paper lists EGA EGAD00001005738, so check whether the raw data are open or controlled. |
| Amato | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 | GEO GSE145996 | 52 patients with exome and RNA-seq. I haven't checked how response is annotated. |
| Jung 2019 | NSCLC, anti-PD-1/PD-L1 | GEO GSE135222 | Only 27 patients (7 durable clinical benefit, 20 non-benefit, using PFS > 180 days). |
| Kim 2018 | Gastric, pembrolizumab | ENA ERP107734 | 61 patients deposited. Downstream papers used only 39–45 because of problems with the expression matrix. |
| IMvigor210 | Urothelial, atezolizumab | R package `IMvigor210CoreBiologies` from research-pub.gene.com/IMvigor210CoreBiologies/ | Processed counts and clinical data, including RECIST response. Papers cite 298 to 348 patients. Raw reads are controlled-access (see below). |

## Needs an application, or has restricted raw data

- **Liu 2019 (melanoma, anti-PD-1):** dbGaP phs000452.v3.p1. One paper says it can also be downloaded from cBioPortal, which would let you skip dbGaP for processed data.
- **Van Allen 2015 (melanoma, anti-CTLA-4):** this is the anti-CTLA-4 cohort you'd want, but I did not confirm its accession. I believe it is also under dbGaP phs000452, so verify that.
- **Miao 2018 (ccRCC):** dbGaP phs001493, controlled access.
- **Mariathasan 2018 (IMvigor210 raw data):** EGA EGAS00001002556, controlled access. The processed package above is enough for most uses.
- **Braun 2020 (nivolumab, ccRCC, CheckMate 025):** EGA EGAS00001004290, EGAS00001004291 and EGAS00001004292. EGA requires a Data Access Committee request. One citing paper describes the deposited data as normalized RNA-seq rather than raw. That description is second-hand.
- **MGH melanoma cohort:** dbGaP phs002683.v1.p1.

## Shortcuts: curated compendia

- **TIDE** (tide.dfci.harvard.edu) hosts processed data from published ICB trials. One comparison table counts about 1,247 patients.
- **CRI iAtlas** has preprocessed expression data in TPM, plus clinical and treatment information. A 2026 preprint downloaded 8 cohorts from it.
- **ICBatlas** (bioinfo.life.hust.edu.cn/ICBatlas/) covers 1,515 samples from 25 studies across nine cancer types. I couldn't confirm that it offers bulk download.
- **Cancer-Immu and ICB-Portal** are compared in the bioRxiv review linked below. Cancer-Immu lists 3,652 patients.

## Practical notes

- **Open-access starting set:** Hugo, Riaz, Gide, Amato, IMvigor210, Kim and Jung. That is four melanoma cohorts plus bladder, gastric and lung. Add Liu and Van Allen (via dbGaP or cBioPortal) for more melanoma, and Braun or Miao for kidney.
- **Pre-treatment samples:** Riaz includes on-treatment biopsies and the MGH GSE115821/GSE168204 cohorts include both timepoints. Keep only pre-treatment samples to avoid leakage.
- **Response definitions:** these differ between cohorts (RECIST, durable clinical benefit by PFS, and so on). Harmonize them before pooling.
- **Batch effects:** the cohorts were run on different platforms and pipelines. Plan to reprocess raw data or use cross-cohort normalization, and validate leave-one-cohort-out.
- **Overlap:** check for patients appearing in more than one cohort before you split train and test sets.
- **Not for your use case:** GSE120575 is single-cell, not bulk.

Prompt

I'm a bioinformatics postdoc building a classifier that predicts response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (anti-PD-1/PD-L1 or anti-CTLA-4) from pre-treatment tumour RNA-seq. I need cohorts of patients who actually received checkpoint inhibitors, with bulk expression data and a recorded clinical response (RECIST or clinical benefit), ideally several independent cohorts so I can validate across studies. Any cancer type is fine. Where can I get these, and which ones can I download right away versus having to apply for?

Please search the web rather than answering from memory, and check that each dataset you recommend really exists and how it can be accessed.

Graders — what "good" means for this case
01-recall-imvigor210llm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the "IMvigor210" cohort (also known as Mariathasan et al. 2018, the atezolizumab anti-PD-L1 trial in metastatic urothelial carcinoma, distributed as the IMvigor210CoreBiologies R package; raw data at EGA under EGAS00001002556) as a candidate dataset for the user's question. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

02-recall-riaz2017llm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the Riaz et al. 2017 melanoma nivolumab cohort (also known as the Riaz cohort, "Tumor and Microenvironment Evolution during Immunotherapy with Nivolumab", samples labelled BMS038109, GEO accession GSE91061, with pre- and on-treatment RNA-seq) as a candidate dataset for the user's question. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

03-recall-hugo2016llm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the Hugo et al. 2016 anti-PD-1 melanoma cohort (also known as the Hugo cohort, "Genomic and Transcriptomic Features of Response to Anti-PD-1 Therapy in Metastatic Melanoma", GEO accession GSE78220, 28 pre-treatment tumours from anti-PD-1-treated patients) as a candidate dataset for the user's question. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

04-recall-gide2019llm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the Gide et al. 2019 melanoma cohort (also known as the Gide cohort, "Distinct Immune Cell Populations Define Response to Anti-PD-1 Monotherapy and Anti-PD-1/Anti-CTLA-4 Combined Therapy", ENA/EBI accession PRJEB23709) as a candidate dataset for the user's question. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

05-access-riaz-geollm

PASS if the final answer mentions the Riaz et al. 2017 nivolumab melanoma cohort (GSE91061) and states, or clearly conveys, that its expression data can be downloaded directly from GEO without any application or data access request (the GEO series includes processed expression files and per-sample response annotations). FAIL if the answer does not mention the Riaz cohort or GSE91061 at all, or says or implies that its expression data require a controlled-access application (for example through dbGaP or EGA) before they can be used.

06-access-imvigor210-packagellm

PASS if the final answer mentions IMvigor210 and states, or clearly conveys, that its processed gene expression data and clinical response annotations can be obtained without an application, through the freely downloadable IMvigor210CoreBiologies R package from Genentech's research-pub site (the package ships under a Creative Commons Attribution licence; mentioning the licence is optional, and other equivalent routes to the same processed data also pass). Adding that the raw sequencing data sit at the European Genome-phenome Archive (EGAS00001002556) under controlled access is correct and does not cause a fail. FAIL if the answer does not mention IMvigor210 at all, or says or implies that IMvigor210 expression data can only be obtained through a controlled-access application (for example only via EGA), or gives no indication of how to obtain it.

07-access-gide-enallm

PASS if the final answer mentions the Gide et al. 2019 melanoma cohort (PRJEB23709) and states, or clearly conveys, that its RNA-seq reads are publicly downloadable from the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA/EBI) without an application or data access request. Saying it is openly available from ENA is enough. FAIL if the answer does not mention the Gide cohort or PRJEB23709 at all, or says or implies that its sequencing data require a controlled-access application.

08-long-tailllm

PASS if the final answer recommends at least one of the following as a candidate data source: (a) the Kim et al. 2018 metastatic gastric cancer pembrolizumab cohort ("Comprehensive molecular characterization of clinical responses to PD-1 inhibition in metastatic gastric cancer", Nature Medicine; ENA accession PRJEB25780); (b) TIGER (Tumor Immunotherapy Gene Expression Resource, a web portal compiling immunotherapy-treated expression cohorts). FAIL if it recommends neither of them.

Four datasets pair chest X-rays with the radiologist's free-text report, and each one exists and has a documented route to the data. I opened the PhysioNet, BIMCV, Stanford AIMI and BRAX pages. I couldn't open the Open-i page, so its download links come from papers and repositories that cite them.

## English

| Dataset | Size | Report content | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| **MIMIC-CXR v2.0.0** | About 377k images and 228k reports from 65k patients (Beth Israel Deaconess ED, 2011–2016) | One de-identified free-text report per study, as `sXXXXXXXX.txt` files and as a single `mimic-cxr-reports` archive | Credentialed PhysioNet access. You register, complete CITI "Data or Specimens Only Research" training, and sign the DUA. You can't share the data and you must release code for any publication that uses it. |
| **CheXpert Plus** | 223,462 image–report pairs, 187,711 studies, 64,725 patients (Stanford, 2002–2017) | Full reports split into up to 11 subsections, plus RadGraph annotations and DICOM and PNG images | Hosted on Redivis through the Stanford AIMI page. The sources say a Research Use Agreement bars commercial use, but I couldn't see the terms text, size or login requirements. Check the Redivis page before planning around it. |
| **IU X-ray (Open-i)** | 3,955 reports and 7,470 images | XML reports with indication, comparison, findings and impression sections | Open download, no credentialing. Reports are at `openi.nlm.nih.gov/imgs/collections/NLMCXR_reports.tgz` and images at `NLMCXR_png.tgz`. Academic Torrents mirrors the reports and a Kaggle mirror has CSVs. The license is reported as CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, which is a secondhand claim. |

- **MIMIC-CXR:** This is the standard benchmark. Its derived versions (MIMIC-CXR-JPG, CXR-PRO and others) also need credentialed access. CXR-PRO removes references to prior studies from the reports, which matters for report generation.
- **CheXpert Plus:** It is the largest set of reports from a single institution outside MIMIC.
- **IU X-ray:** It is small, so it works for quick experiments and as a second test set. Some papers report slightly different counts, for example after dropping reports with no findings section. Check the license text yourself, since I only have it from papers.

## Non-English

- **PadChest (Spanish):** It has more than 160k images from 67k patients at Hospital San Juan in Spain, from 2009 to 2017. The reports are in Spanish. The full dataset is about 1 TB and is free for researchers. You request it through a form on the BIMCV page and agree to its Research Use Agreement, which bars sharing and re-identification. A 167 MB sample is on Kaggle, but I couldn't confirm whether it includes report text.
- **PadChest-GR:** It has 4,555 studies with bilingual Spanish and English reports and grounding annotations. It is available on request from BIMCV. That makes it the only bilingual option I found.
- **BIMCV COVID-19+:** It has Spanish reports, but it is small and limited to COVID-19 patients. I didn't check its access terms.

## Datasets to avoid

- **BRAX (Brazilian Portuguese):** It releases only the 14 labels derived from the reports. The paper says free-text reports are not provided in the current version.
- **German:** I found no public German set with reports. The only one that came up (Hannover COVID-19) is 240 images, with no reports mentioned.
- **CX-CHR (Chinese reports):** It is private.

## Suggested plan

Start with IU X-ray because it needs no approval. Apply for MIMIC-CXR credentialing at the same time, since it takes the longest. Request PadChest for the non-English experiment.

Sources:
- [MIMIC-CXR v2.0.0 (PhysioNet)](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-cxr/2.0.0/)
- [MIMIC-CXR paper (Scientific Data)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-019-0322-0)
- [CheXpert Plus (Stanford AIMI)](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/chexpert-plus)
- [CheXpert Plus paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.19538)
- [PadChest (BIMCV)](https://bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest/)
- [PadChest paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.07441)
- [PadChest-GR](https://ai.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/AIdbp2401120)
- [BIMCV COVID-19+](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.01174)
- [BRAX paper](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9364309/)
- [IU X-ray on Academic Torrents](https://academictorrents.com/details/66450ba52ba3f83fbf82ef9c91f2bde0e845aba9)
- [IU X-ray usage in PLOS ONE](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0259639)

Judge votes✓ ✓ ✓
Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
These are the datasets that pair chest X-rays with the radiologist's actual report text. I checked each one against search results. I didn't open every access form, so the gaps are noted below.

## English

| Dataset | Size | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **[MIMIC-CXR v2.1.0](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-cxr/2.1.0/)** | About 377k images and 227k studies. Reports are one text file per study, plus a single `mimic-cxr-reports.tar.gz`. | PhysioNet credentialed access. You register, complete credentialing, and sign the data use agreement. |
| **[CheXpert Plus](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/chexpert-plus)** | About 223k image-report pairs across 187,711 studies. Reports are split into 11 subsections, including history, findings and impression. | Stanford AIMI Research Use Agreement. Code and models are in [Stanford-AIMI/chexpert-plus](https://github.com/Stanford-AIMI/chexpert-plus). |
| **[ReXGradient-160K](https://huggingface.co/datasets/rajpurkarlab/ReXGradient-160K)** | 160k studies and 273k images from 3 US institutions. The paper is [arXiv 2505.00228](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00228). | You sign a license on Hugging Face. |
| **IU X-Ray (Open-i)** | 7,470 images and 3,955 reports. | Public download of PNG or DICOM images and XML reports from [NLM Open-i](https://openi.nlm.nih.gov/faq). A [Kaggle mirror](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/raddar/chest-xrays-indiana-university) also exists. |

- **MIMIC-CXR:** This is the standard benchmark, so use it if you need results comparable to published work. The PhysioNet data use agreement appears to restrict sending the data to external LLM services. One derived dataset said it used an agreement-compliant setup for LLM processing. Read the terms before you use API-based models.
- **CheXpert Plus:** One study notes that the official test split is only 200 studies, so you may need your own splits.
- **ReXGradient-160K:** I only saw the Hugging Face license-gating step. I didn't see the license terms.
- **IU X-Ray:** It's small but easy to get, which makes it good for quick prototyping. The common split is 2,770 / 395 / 790 reports for train / val / test. A third-party catalog lists its license as "none provided", so check NLM's terms before redistributing.

## Non-English (secondary experiment)

- **[PadChest](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.07441)** has Spanish reports, with more than 160k images from 67k patients at San Juan Hospital. It is hosted by BIMCV at `bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest/`.
  - You request access through a form on that page and agree not to share the data or re-identify patients.
  - About 27% of the labels were manually annotated and the rest came from a model. That doesn't affect the report text itself.
  - I didn't find approval times or eligibility rules.
- **PadChest-GR** has 4,555 studies with grounded reports in both English and Spanish. It is available on request at `bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest-gr/`. It is small, but the bilingual reports are useful.
- **[BIMCV COVID-19+](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.01174)** has Spanish reports, but it is small (about 2,400 radiographs) and COVID-focused. It is also available on request from BIMCV.

## What I couldn't confirm

- I didn't open the BIMCV pages, so confirm their current status and forms yourself.
- My searches for Rad-ReStruct and CTRG returned nothing, so I'm not recommending them. CTRG may be a Chinese-language report set, but I couldn't verify that.
- Chinese, German and other non-English chest X-ray report sets may exist, but I didn't search for them. I can look if you want a language other than Spanish.

I'd start with IU X-Ray while you wait for MIMIC-CXR credentialing, which is usually the slowest step. CheXpert Plus and ReXGradient add scale.

- [MIMIC-CXR v2.1.0](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-cxr/2.1.0/)

- [MIMIC-CXR-JPG](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-cxr-jpg/2.1.0/)
- [NLM Open-i FAQ](https://openi.nlm.nih.gov/faq)

These are the datasets that pair chest X-rays with the radiologist's actual report text. I checked each one against search results. I didn't open every access form, so the gaps are noted below.

## English

| Dataset | Size | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **[MIMIC-CXR v2.1.0](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-cxr/2.1.0/)** | About 377k images and 227k studies. Reports are one text file per study, plus a single `mimic-cxr-reports.tar.gz`. | PhysioNet credentialed access. You register, complete credentialing, and sign the data use agreement. |
| **[CheXpert Plus](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/chexpert-plus)** | About 223k image-report pairs across 187,711 studies. Reports are split into 11 subsections, including history, findings and impression. | Stanford AIMI Research Use Agreement. Code and models are in [Stanford-AIMI/chexpert-plus](https://github.com/Stanford-AIMI/chexpert-plus). |
| **[ReXGradient-160K](https://huggingface.co/datasets/rajpurkarlab/ReXGradient-160K)** | 160k studies and 273k images from 3 US institutions. The paper is [arXiv 2505.00228](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00228). | You sign a license on Hugging Face. |
| **IU X-Ray (Open-i)** | 7,470 images and 3,955 reports. | Public download of PNG or DICOM images and XML reports from [NLM Open-i](https://openi.nlm.nih.gov/faq). A [Kaggle mirror](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/raddar/chest-xrays-indiana-university) also exists. |

- **MIMIC-CXR:** This is the standard benchmark, so use it if you need results comparable to published work. The PhysioNet data use agreement appears to restrict sending the data to external LLM services. One derived dataset said it used an agreement-compliant setup for LLM processing. Read the terms before you use API-based models.
- **CheXpert Plus:** One study notes that the official test split is only 200 studies, so you may need your own splits.
- **ReXGradient-160K:** I only saw the Hugging Face license-gating step. I didn't see the license terms.
- **IU X-Ray:** It's small but easy to get, which makes it good for quick prototyping. The common split is 2,770 / 395 / 790 reports for train / val / test. A third-party catalog lists its license as "none provided", so check NLM's terms before redistributing.

## Non-English (secondary experiment)

- **[PadChest](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.07441)** has Spanish reports, with more than 160k images from 67k patients at San Juan Hospital. It is hosted by BIMCV at `bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest/`.
  - You request access through a form on that page and agree not to share the data or re-identify patients.
  - About 27% of the labels were manually annotated and the rest came from a model. That doesn't affect the report text itself.
  - I didn't find approval times or eligibility rules.
- **PadChest-GR** has 4,555 studies with grounded reports in both English and Spanish. It is available on request at `bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest-gr/`. It is small, but the bilingual reports are useful.
- **[BIMCV COVID-19+](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.01174)** has Spanish reports, but it is small (about 2,400 radiographs) and COVID-focused. It is also available on request from BIMCV.

## What I couldn't confirm

- I didn't open the BIMCV pages, so confirm their current status and forms yourself.
- My searches for Rad-ReStruct and CTRG returned nothing, so I'm not recommending them. CTRG may be a Chinese-language report set, but I couldn't verify that.
- Chinese, German and other non-English chest X-ray report sets may exist, but I didn't search for them. I can look if you want a language other than Spanish.

I'd start with IU X-Ray while you wait for MIMIC-CXR credentialing, which is usually the slowest step. CheXpert Plus and ReXGradient add scale.

These datasets pair chest X-rays with the radiologist's free-text report. I confirmed each one exists, but the access details come from search snippets and the one page I could fetch. Several pages I didn't open directly, so check the exact terms before you apply.

## English

| Dataset | Size | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **MIMIC-CXR** (v2.1.0) | ~377k radiographs, ~228k reports | Credentialed PhysioNet access |
| **CheXpert Plus** | ~223k image–report pairs, 187,711 studies, 64,725 patients | Stanford AIMI data use agreement |
| **IU X-ray (Open-i)** | ~3,955 reports, ~7,470 images | Open download |

- **MIMIC-CXR:** The DICOM images come with free-text reports from routine care. The reports are also bundled in one archive, `mimic-cxr-reports.tar.gz`. To get access you register on PhysioNet, complete credentialing, and sign the data use agreement. The license is the PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License 1.5.0. This is the standard main benchmark. Plan for some lead time on credentialing. Don't confuse it with MIMIC-CXR-JPG, which has JPGs and labels derived from the reports.
- **CheXpert Plus:** The reports are split into 11 subsections, and the DICOMs come with metadata and demographics. You download it from the AIMI page after agreeing to the research use agreement. A secondary source says the agreement prohibits commercial use and redistribution. The sources disagree on the exact image count (223,228 vs 223,462), so check the version you download.
- **IU X-ray (Open-i):** Reports have indication, findings and impression sections, and are annotated with MeSH and RadLex codes. The image and report archives (`NLMCXR_png.tgz`, `NLMCXR_reports.tgz`) are listed on the NLM Open-i site. There is also a Kaggle copy, `raddar/chest-xrays-indiana-university`. It is small, so people usually use it as a secondary benchmark next to MIMIC-CXR. Different papers cite slightly different counts.

## Non-English

| Dataset | Language | Size | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PadChest** | Spanish | >160k images, ~109k reports | Request form to BIMCV |
| **PadChest-GR** | English and Spanish | 4,555 studies | Request on BIMCV site |
| **ViX-Ray** | Vietnamese | 5,400 samples | Hugging Face, not gated |
| **CASIA-CXR** | French | 11,111 images | Download from the project site |

- **PadChest:** You request access at the BIMCV project page and agree not to share the data or try to re-identify patients. I couldn't find the form fields or the typical approval time. Many of its labels were extracted automatically from the reports, but the reports themselves are included.
- **PadChest-GR:** It is a curated subset with grounded reports in both languages. That makes it useful if you want English and Spanish together, but it is small.
- **ViX-Ray:** It has 4,320 train, 540 validation and 540 test samples. Each is a PA-view image with Vietnamese findings and impressions. I fetched the page and it shows no gating. The license is inconsistent: the tag says CC BY-NC 4.0 and the description says CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. It is 17.3 GB.
- **CASIA-CXR:** It has frontal radiographs with French reports, but only for five conditions: cardiomegaly, pneumothorax, pleural effusion, pneumonia and mass. The authors say it is freely available at casia-cxr.net, and there is a Hugging Face mirror (`FrancophonIA/CASIA-CXR`). I couldn't open the paper page to confirm the license.

## Not usable
- **Chinese:** CX-CHR and CH-Xray are private. COV-CTR is public but covers CT, not X-ray.
- **German:** The only corpus I found is a private one from University Hospital Bonn, used for report labeling. I found no public German set.
- **Arabic:** I found none.
- **VinDr-CXR:** It has radiologist annotations and labels, not free-text reports.

## Suggested setup
Start the MIMIC-CXR credentialing now, since it is the slowest step. Meanwhile, prototype on IU X-ray, which needs no approval. Add CheXpert Plus as a second large English set. For the secondary experiment, PadChest (Spanish) is the largest non-English option but needs approval. ViX-Ray or CASIA-CXR are the quickest to get, though both are small.

- [MIMIC-CXR paper (Scientific Data)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-019-0322-0)
- [CheXpert Plus (Stanford AIMI)](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/chexpert-plus)
- [CheXpert Plus paper (arXiv)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.19538)
- [IU X-ray overview (Awesome-Medical-Dataset)](https://github.com/openmedlab/Awesome-Medical-Dataset/blob/main/resources/IU-Xray.md)
- [PadChest paper (arXiv)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.07441)
- [PadChest-GR](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/392806493_PadChest-GR_A_Bilingual_Chest_X-Ray_Dataset_for_Grounded_Radiology_Report_Generation)
- [ViX-Ray on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/MilitaryHospital175/VNMedical_bv175)

- [CASIA-CXR on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/FrancophonIA/CASIA-CXR)

Prompt

I'm working on automatic radiology report generation for chest X-rays, so I need datasets where each image or study comes with the actual free-text report the radiologist wrote, not just labels extracted from it. English reports are preferred, but a non-English set would be fine for a secondary experiment. Which datasets have that, and what's involved in getting each of them?

Please search the web rather than answering from memory, and check that each dataset you recommend really exists and how it can be accessed.

Graders — what "good" means for this case
01-recall-mimic-cxrllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the "MIMIC-CXR" dataset (also written MIMIC CXR; chest radiographs with free-text radiology reports from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, about 377,000 images from about 228,000 studies, on PhysioNet; MIMIC-CXR-JPG counts when used together with the MIMIC-CXR reports) as a candidate dataset for the user's question, in any version. FAIL if the answer does not mention MIMIC-CXR, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

02-recall-iu-xrayllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the Indiana University chest X-ray collection (also known as IU X-ray, IU-Xray, the Open-i chest X-ray collection, OpenI, or NLMCXR; about 7,470 images with 3,955 radiology reports from the Indiana Network for Patient Care, distributed by the US National Library of Medicine's Open-i service) as a candidate dataset for the user's question. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

03-recall-padchestllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the "PadChest" dataset (more than 160,000 chest X-rays with Spanish-language radiology reports from Hospital San Juan, Alicante, distributed by BIMCV; Bustos et al. 2020) as a candidate dataset for the user's question, for example as the non-English option. FAIL if the answer does not mention PadChest, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

04-access-mimic-cxr-credentialingllm

PASS if the final answer mentions MIMIC-CXR and states, or clearly conveys, that access requires becoming a credentialed PhysioNet user, completing the required human-subjects research training (CITI "Data or Specimens Only Research") and signing the PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement before the files, including the reports, can be downloaded. Naming the main steps (credentialing plus training plus data use agreement) or describing it as "credentialed access requiring training and a signed DUA" passes. FAIL if the answer does not mention MIMIC-CXR at all, or says or implies that MIMIC-CXR or its reports can be downloaded without credentialing, or gives no indication of the approval steps.

05-access-iu-xray-downloadllm

PASS if the final answer mentions the Indiana University chest X-ray collection (IU X-ray, Open-i, NLMCXR) and states, or clearly conveys, that its images and reports can be downloaded directly without registration or an application (for example from the National Library of Medicine's Open-i site, where it is released under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 licence; pointing to a public mirror also passes). Mentioning the non-commercial licence is optional. FAIL if the answer does not mention this collection at all, or says or implies that it requires credentialing, an application or a data use agreement.

06-access-padchest-requestllm

PASS if the final answer mentions PadChest and states, or clearly conveys, that it is free for researchers but the full dataset is obtained by submitting an access request form to BIMCV and accepting the PadChest research use agreement (committing not to share the data and not to try to re-identify people), rather than by an anonymous direct download. Wording such as "free, request access through BIMCV's form" passes. FAIL if the answer does not mention PadChest at all, or says or implies that the full PadChest dataset can be downloaded with no request or agreement, or gives no indication of how it is obtained.

07-trap-chestxray14llm

PASS if the final answer does not present the NIH ChestX-ray14 dataset (also called ChestX-ray8, NIH Chest X-ray Dataset, or NIH CXR14, from the NIH Clinical Center) as providing free-text radiology reports. The user needs the radiologist's free-text report for each image; for ChestX-ray14 the original radiology reports are not available, and only labels text-mined from them were released. Not mentioning it passes; mentioning it while making clear it has labels but no reports passes. FAIL if the answer says ChestX-ray14 includes radiology reports, or lists it among datasets that meet the free-text report requirement without noting that its reports were not released.

08-long-tailllm

PASS if the final answer recommends at least one of the following as a candidate dataset: (a) CheXpert Plus (Stanford AIMI; about 223,000 chest X-ray and radiology report pairs from about 65,000 patients, released in 2024); (b) PadChest-GR (PadChest Grounded-Reporting, a grounded radiology report generation dataset derived from PadChest); (c) ReXGradient-160K (a 2025 dataset of 160,000 chest X-ray studies with paired radiology reports from 109,487 patients across three US health systems, distributed on Hugging Face). FAIL if it recommends none of them.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Four public datasets fit your criteria. I checked each one's page where I could. I haven't downloaded anything or counted images myself.

## Best fits

**1. DDI (Diverse Dermatology Images, Stanford)**
- **Contents:** 656 clinical images from 570 patients. Every lesion is biopsy-proven, with 78 disease labels plus a benign/malignant flag.
- **Dark-skin coverage:** 207 images are Fitzpatrick V–VI, which is 159 benign and 48 malignant. The other bins are 208 for I–II and 241 for III–IV. This is the most balanced of the datasets.
- **Limits:**
  - Skin tone comes in three bins (I–II, III–IV, V–VI), so you can't separate V from VI.
  - It is small, so subgroup confidence intervals will be wide.
  - Those labels were validated by two dermatologists, which makes them stronger than most.
- **Access:** You download it from the Stanford AIMI portal. Registration is required, and you must accept a Research Use Agreement. The terms are non-commercial research only, no redistribution, no derivative works and no sharing the link. A Redivis mirror also exists. I couldn't open its page, so I don't know whether that route has the same terms.
- **Links:** [project page](https://ddi-dataset.github.io), [Redivis listing](https://stanford.redivis.com/datasets/3r16-5mby7gfer), [paper](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.abq6147)

**2. SCIN (Google)**
- **Contents:** About 10,400 images from about 5,000 contributions. They are crowdsourced US clinical photos with dermatologist condition labels. It has estimated Fitzpatrick type (eFST), layperson-estimated Monk tone (eMST) and some self-reported Fitzpatrick type. It's the only option here with Monk labels.
- **Dark-skin coverage:** The demo notebook output shows self-reported FST5 at 214 and FST6 at 143. Those are about 8.5% and 5.7% of the roughly 2,500 contributors who self-reported. That denominator is my inference. I couldn't get the eFST or eMST tables, so I can't give counts for V–VI or Monk 8–10 on the estimated labels. Table S11 of the paper suggests Monk 10 is nearly absent.
- **Limits:**
  - Diagnoses are dermatologist opinions from photos, not biopsy results, and some images have several or uncertain labels.
  - The Monk labels come from nonclinical labelers in two geographies and differ between them. The schema has separate US and India label columns.
  - Check how many images per tone survive your gradability filters.
- **Access:** Open Google Cloud Storage bucket `dx-scin-public-data`. `scin_demo.ipynb` shows how to load it. The SCIN Data Use License applies, so read it before use.
- **Links:** [GitHub](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin), [paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18545), [schema](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin/blob/main/dataset_schema.md)

**3. Fitzpatrick17k**
- **Contents:** 16,577 clinical images with Fitzpatrick I–VI labels and 100+ conditions, scraped from the DermaAmin and Atlas Dermatologico atlases.
- **Dark-skin coverage:** One review reports only 635 images of type VI. I didn't verify that or the type V count.
- **Limits:**
  - It has duplicates and label errors, and the Fitzpatrick labels were annotated rather than clinically assessed.
  - Diagnoses are not biopsy-confirmed.
  - Use it as a large supplement, not as your main benchmark.
- **Access:** `fitzpatrick17k.csv` is on GitHub. The images must be downloaded from the URLs in the CSV, and some links are broken. You can instead fill out the maintainers' form to get a link to all the images. The license is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.
- **Link:** [GitHub](https://github.com/mattgroh/fitzpatrick17k)

## Worth considering, but not fully verified
- **PASSION:** 4,901 images from 1,653 patients in Sub-Saharan Africa. It is mostly pediatric (eczema, fungal infections, scabies, impetigo), so it is a narrow condition set that probably has many dark-skin images. I couldn't find the Fitzpatrick distribution, the download location or the license. Check [passionderm.github.io](https://passionderm.github.io) and the [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04584).
- **DermaCon-IN:** A search summary says 5,450 images from India with both Fitzpatrick and Monk labels. I didn't open it, so confirm that it exists, how to access it and the tone distribution before relying on it.

## Not suitable
**PAD-UFES-20** has CC BY 4.0 licensing and clinical metadata, but only 579 of 1,373 patients have Fitzpatrick type recorded and just one image is type VI.

## Suggested setup
Use DDI as the primary benchmark because its labels are biopsy-proven and its V–VI group is large. Add SCIN for Monk-scale analysis and more conditions. Fitzpatrick17k can serve as a large, noisier robustness check. Keep in mind that Fitzpatrick and Monk labels measure different things, and that SCIN's labels are estimated from photos.

Sources:
- [Skin Type Diversity in Skin Lesion Datasets: A Review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11343783/)
- [PASSION for Dermatology (arXiv)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.04584)
- [SCIN GitHub](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)
- [SCIN paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18545)
- [SCIN demo notebook](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin/blob/main/scin_demo.ipynb)
- [DDI, Science Advances](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.abq6147)
- [DDI project page](https://ddi-dataset.github.io)
- [DDI on Redivis](https://stanford.redivis.com/datasets/3r16-5mby7gfer)
- [Fitzpatrick17k GitHub](https://github.com/mattgroh/fitzpatrick17k)

That denominator is my inference. I couldn't get the eFST or eMST tables, so I can't give counts for V–VI or Monk 8–10 on the estimated labels. Table S11 of the paper suggests Monk 10 is nearly absent.
- **Limits:**
  - Diagnoses are dermatologist opinions from photos, not biopsy results, and some images have several or uncertain labels.
  - The Monk labels come from nonclinical labelers in two geographies and differ between them. The schema has separate US and India label columns.
  - Check how many images per tone survive your gradability filters.
- **Access:** Open Google Cloud Storage bucket `dx-scin-public-data`. `scin_demo.ipynb` shows how to load it. The SCIN Data Use License applies, so read it before use.
- **Links:** [GitHub](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin), [paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18545), [schema](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin/blob/main/dataset_schema.md)

- **Contents:** 16,577 clinical images with Fitzpatrick I–VI labels and 100+ conditions, scraped from the DermaAmin and Atlas Dermatologico atlases.

  - It has duplicates and label errors, and the Fitzpatrick labels were annotated rather than clinically assessed.

- **PASSION:** 4,901 images from 1,653 patients in Sub-Saharan Africa. Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Four public datasets fit your criteria. I checked each one's access page, except where I say otherwise. I haven't downloaded any of them or counted any images myself. Every V/VI figure below is from papers or secondary sources.

## Best fits

**1. Diverse Dermatology Images (DDI), Stanford**
- **What it is:** 656 clinical images from 570 patients. Diagnoses are pathology-confirmed, and each image has a malignant/non-malignant label.
- **Skin tone labels:** Fitzpatrick I–VI. Two board-certified dermatologists assigned them, using the in-person clinic evaluation and the demographic photos.
- **V/VI representation:** This is the most balanced set. One secondary source reports 207 images of types V–VI (159 benign, 48 malignant). Another reports 81 with 16 malignant. I couldn't reconcile the two, so check the counts in the metadata yourself.
- **Access:** Register on the [DDI site](https://ddi-dataset.github.io/) through the Stanford AIMI portal. Each user registers individually.
- **Terms:** Non-commercial research use only. No redistribution, and no derivative works.
- **Fit for your audit:** The set is small, so confidence intervals will be wide. It was built to be matched across tone groups (diagnostic category, age, gender, photo date), which suits an audit.

**2. SCIN (Google)**
- **What it is:** 10,000+ crowdsourced clinical photos from US users, with self-reported demographics and dermatologist condition labels.
- **Skin tone labels:** It is the only dataset here with both scales. It has self-reported Fitzpatrick, estimated Fitzpatrick and estimated Monk Skin Tone. The Monk labels come from laypeople, not dermatologists.
- **Access:** The `dx-scin-public-data` Google Cloud Storage bucket. The [GitHub repo](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin) has a demo notebook and a schema file. It is released under the SCIN Data Use License.
- **Caveats:** About 89% of the diagnosable cases are allergic, infectious or inflammatory conditions, so it has little skin cancer. Labels are differential diagnoses, not biopsy-confirmed. The repo lists known issues: duplicate images, 48 gradable cases with no condition label, and one missing file. I couldn't find V/VI counts on the page, so count them from the metadata.

**3. Fitzpatrick 17k**
- **What it is:** 16,577 clinical images across 114 conditions, with Fitzpatrick I–VI labels from Scale AI annotators. This is by far the largest set.
- **V/VI representation:** About 13% of images are V+VI. A review puts type VI alone at 635 images.
- **Access:** The [GitHub repo](https://github.com/mattgroh/fitzpatrick17k) has `fitzpatrick17k.csv` with labels and URLs. You download the images from the original atlas sites, and some links are broken. The authors offer a form to request a link to all the images.
- **Terms:** CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.
- **Caveats:** Diagnoses come from atlas metadata, not histopathology. Near-duplicate pairs exist, some with conflicting labels. Skin tone labels are subjective. Deduplicate and consider the label noise before drawing fairness conclusions.

**4. DermaCon-IN**
- **What it is:** 5,450 images of Indian patients with 245 disease labels, annotated for both Fitzpatrick and Monk.
- **Access:** [Harvard Dataverse](https://dataverse.harvard.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.7910/DVN/W7OUZM), about 4 GB, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The [paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.06099) says the code is on GitHub. I confirmed the access details from the paper, not by opening the Dataverse page.
- **Caveats:** I couldn't read the per-tone counts. The paper says the intro covers Fitzpatrick IV–VI but the text also says Fitzpatrick 3–4, so V/VI coverage is unclear. It is a single-country population.

## Ruled out or weak
- **PAD-UFES-20:** Fitzpatrick labels exist for only 579 of 1,373 patients, and one source counts just 11 images of type V–VI. It doesn't meet your "not a handful" requirement.
- **HAM10000, ISIC 2020, MILK10k:** These have no reliable skin tone labels, and fewer than 1% of subjects are V/VI. One paper trained models to estimate tone for them. That gives you estimated labels, not ground truth.
- **Monk Skin Tone Examples and Skin Tone in the Wild:** These carry Monk labels but aren't dermatology data.

## Suggested approach
Use DDI as the main audit set because its labels are the cleanest. Use Fitzpatrick 17k for statistical power, and SCIN if you want Monk labels or inflammatory conditions. All of these have non-commercial terms, so check that they cover your audit's use.

Sources:
- [Fitzpatrick17k overview](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/fitzpatrick-17k-dataset)
- [Skin Type Diversity in Skin Lesion Datasets: A Review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11343783/)
- [SCIN GitHub](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)
- [DDI dataset page](https://ddi-dataset.github.io/)
- [Fitzpatrick17k GitHub](https://github.com/mattgroh/fitzpatrick17k)
- [DermaCon-IN paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.06099)
- [Pipsqueak / skin tone bias in melanoma detection](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1877750326000761)
- [Skin Tone Label Granularity paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.11184)

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Four public datasets fit. I fetched the access page for each one, except where noted.

| Dataset | Skin tone label | Diagnosis | Dark-skin representation | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DDI** (Stanford) | Fitzpatrick, grouped I–II, III–IV, V–VI | Biopsy-confirmed, with benign/malignant and disease labels | 207 of 656 images are V–VI (208 I–II, 241 III–IV). Images come from 570 patients. | Free registration and a research-use agreement through the Stanford AIMI portal. Non-commercial, no redistribution. |
| **SCIN** (Google) | Self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick, and layperson-estimated Monk | Dermatologist condition labels for 2,835 of 5,033 contributions | V–VI is 16.4% by self-report but only 5.8% by dermatologist estimate. Monk 8–10 is under 1.5%. | Google Cloud Storage bucket `dx-scin-public-data` under the SCIN Data Use License. The repo has a demo notebook. |
| **Fitzpatrick17k** | Fitzpatrick I–VI | 114 conditions, with a 3-class label | V–VI is 467 of the 3,230 images in the SkinCon-annotated subset. I couldn't find counts for the full 16,577. | The CSV is on GitHub under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. The images are not included. |
| **DermaCon-IN** | Fitzpatrick and Monk, per image | 88 main classes, 19 subclasses, 245 fine-grained labels | Mostly darker skin (Fitzpatrick IV–VI, Monk 4–9). I found no per-type counts. | Harvard Dataverse, DOI [10.7910/DVN/W7OUZM](https://dataverse.harvard.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.7910/DVN/W7OUZM), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, about 4 GB. |

**Which to use**
- **DDI is the cleanest for your question.** It has reliable diagnoses, it's roughly balanced across tones, and it was built to compare I–II with V–VI. Its limit is size, so confidence intervals on V–VI will be wide.
- **SCIN has Monk labels.** Its Fitzpatrick V–VI share depends heavily on which label you use. Its diagnoses are mostly inflammatory or allergic conditions (89% of the 2,835 with a differential), not cancer. Only about half the contributions have a self-reported skin type. The paper's two Monk labeler groups also disagree on the same images.
- **Fitzpatrick17k is the largest.** Its diagnoses come from online atlases rather than biopsy, with more than 30% label noise reported. It has about 3.6 times more light than dark samples. Many image links are broken, and the authors ask you to fill out a form for a full set of links.
- **DermaCon-IN adds a different population** (South India). Its Fitzpatrick breakdown is only in a figure, and its text is inconsistent about whether the annotations centre on type 3–4 or IV–VI. Check the actual label counts before relying on it.

**Not recommended yet**
- A 2024 MSKCC skin-tone labeling set has 4,879 dermoscopic images from 64 patients, with Fitzpatrick, Monk and colorimeter labels (CC BY). The listing didn't say whether it has diagnosis labels, and I didn't open the dataset page, so I can't confirm it fits.
- None of these is dermoscopy-only. If you need dermoscopy with tone labels, I didn't find a verified one.

Per-type counts for SCIN and DermaCon-IN need to be computed from the data itself.

Sources:
- [SCIN on GitHub](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)
- [SCIN paper (arXiv 2402.18545)](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.18545v1)
- [Fitzpatrick17k on GitHub](https://github.com/mattgroh/fitzpatrick17k)
- [DDI dataset page](https://ddi-dataset.github.io/)
- [DDI paper (Science Advances)](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.abq6147)
- [SkinCon (arXiv 2302.00785)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.00785)
- [DermaCon-IN (arXiv 2506.06099)](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.06099)
- [Skin lesion dataset catalog](https://github.com/AxDante/skin-lesion-dataset-analysis)

| **DDI** (Stanford) | Fitzpatrick, grouped I–II, III–IV, V–VI | Biopsy-confirmed, with benign/malignant and disease labels | 207 of 656 images are V–VI (208 I–II, 241 III–IV). Images come from 570 patients. | Free registration and a research-use agreement through the Stanford AIMI portal. Non-commercial, no redistribution. |
| **SCIN** (Google) | Self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick, and layperson-estimated Monk | Dermatologist condition labels for 2,835 of 5,033 contributions | V–VI is 16.4% by self-report but only 5.8% by dermatologist estimate. Monk 8–10 is under 1.5%. | Google Cloud Storage bucket `dx-scin-public-data` under the SCIN Data Use License. The repo has a demo notebook. |
| **Fitzpatrick17k** | Fitzpatrick I–VI | 114 conditions, with a 3-class label | V–VI is 467 of the 3,230 images in the SkinCon-annotated subset. I couldn't find counts for the full 16,577. | The CSV is on GitHub under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. The images are not included. |
| **DermaCon-IN** | Fitzpatrick and Monk, per image | 88 main classes, 19 subclasses, 245 fine-grained labels | Mostly darker skin (Fitzpatrick IV–VI, Monk 4–9). I found no per-type counts. | Harvard Dataverse, DOI [10.7910/DVN/W7OUZM](https://dataverse.harvard.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.7910/DVN/W7OUZM), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, about 4 GB. |

**Which to use**
- **DDI is the cleanest for your question.** It has reliable diagnoses, it's roughly balanced across tones, and it was built to compare I–II with V–VI. Its limit is size, so confidence intervals on V–VI will be wide.
- **SCIN has Monk labels.** Its Fitzpatrick V–VI share depends heavily on which label you use. Its diagnoses are mostly inflammatory or allergic conditions (89% of the 2,835 with a differential), not cancer. Only about half the contributions have a self-reported skin type. The paper's two Monk labeler groups also disagree on the same images.
- **Fitzpatrick17k is the largest.** Its diagnoses come from online atlases rather than biopsy, with more than 30% label noise reported. It has about 3.6 times more light than dark samples. Many image links are broken, and the authors ask you to fill out a form for a full set of links.
- **DermaCon-IN adds a different population** (South India). Its Fitzpatrick breakdown is only in a figure, and its text is inconsistent about whether the annotations centre on type 3–4 or IV–VI. Check the actual label counts before relying on it.

**Not recommended yet**
- A 2024 MSKCC skin-tone labeling set has 4,879 dermoscopic images from 64 patients, with Fitzpatrick, Monk and colorimeter labels (CC BY). The listing didn't say whether it has diagnosis labels, and I didn't open the dataset page, so I can't confirm it fits.
- None of these is dermoscopy-only. If you need dermoscopy with tone labels, I didn't find a verified one.

Per-type counts for SCIN and DermaCon-IN need to be computed from the data itself.

Prompt

For a fairness audit I want to test whether dermatology image classifiers do worse on darker skin. I need skin images where every image (or patient) comes with a skin tone label, either Fitzpatrick type or Monk scale, as well as a diagnosis, and the darker types (V and VI) have to actually be represented rather than a handful. Clinical photos or dermoscopy are both fine, and it doesn't have to be skin cancer only. Which public datasets have that?

Please search the web rather than answering from memory, and check that each dataset you recommend really exists and how it can be accessed.

Graders — what "good" means for this case
01-recall-fitzpatrick17kllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the "Fitzpatrick17k" dataset (also written Fitzpatrick 17k or F17k; about 16,577 clinical dermatology images from the DermaAmin and Atlas Dermatologico atlases, each annotated with a Fitzpatrick skin type, by Groh et al. 2021) as a candidate dataset for the user's question, in any version. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

02-recall-ddillm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the "Diverse Dermatology Images" dataset (also known as DDI or the Stanford DDI dataset; about 656 clinical images balanced across Fitzpatrick skin types I-II, III-IV and V-VI, by Daneshjou et al. 2022, distributed by the Stanford AIMI center) as a candidate dataset for the user's question. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

03-recall-scinllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the "SCIN" dataset (Skin Condition Image Network, also called the Google SCIN dataset; more than 10,000 crowdsourced images of common skin conditions from over 5,000 US contributors, with self-reported and dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick skin type and estimated Monk Skin Tone labels, by Ward et al. 2024) as a candidate dataset for the user's question. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

04-access-ddi-registrationllm

PASS if the final answer mentions the Diverse Dermatology Images (DDI) dataset and states, or clearly conveys, that obtaining it requires registering for the download (through the Stanford AIMI center's sharing site) and agreeing to a research use agreement that limits use to non-commercial research. Wording such as "free, but you must register and accept a data use or research use agreement" passes. FAIL if the answer does not mention DDI at all, or says or implies that DDI can be downloaded anonymously with no registration and no agreement to terms.

05-access-scin-downloadllm

PASS if the final answer mentions the SCIN (Skin Condition Image Network) dataset and states, or clearly conveys, that it is openly downloadable without an application or approval step (it is hosted in a public Google Cloud Storage bucket linked from its GitHub repository and released under the SCIN Data Use License). FAIL if the answer does not mention SCIN at all, or says or implies that SCIN requires an application, credentialing, institutional approval or a request to the authors.

06-trap-ham10000llm

PASS if the final answer does not present the HAM10000 dataset ("Human Against Machine with 10000 training images", also distributed as the ISIC 2018 Task 3 training set) as providing skin tone labels. The user needs a Fitzpatrick or Monk skin tone label for each image; HAM10000's metadata contain lesion and image IDs, diagnosis, diagnosis method, age, sex, body site and source collection, but no skin type field. Not mentioning HAM10000 passes; mentioning it while saying it lacks skin tone labels (for example, usable only if the user estimates skin tone themselves) passes. FAIL if the answer says HAM10000 includes Fitzpatrick or other skin tone labels, or lists it among the datasets that meet the skin tone label requirement without noting that it has no such labels.

07-long-tailllm

PASS if the final answer recommends at least one of the following as a candidate dataset: (a) PASSION ("PASSION for Dermatology", Gottfrois et al., MICCAI 2024; about 4,901 images of common paediatric skin conditions from 1,653 patients in Sub-Saharan Africa, mostly Fitzpatrick types V and VI); (b) DermaCon-IN (a 2025 dataset of about 5,450 clinical images from about 3,000 outpatients in South India, with Fitzpatrick and Monk skin tone ratings, released on Harvard Dataverse). FAIL if it recommends neither of them.

Three datasets fit, and all are on PhysioNet as open access (CC BY 4.0). The PhysioNet pages for each say "Anyone can access the files, as long as they conform to the terms of the specified license." That means no account, credentialing, or data use agreement. I checked the pages for all three, but I haven't downloaded anything.

## Recommendations

**1. PTB-XL (best for cardiologist labels)**
- **Size:** 21,799 ten-second, 12-lead ECGs from 18,869 patients, about 3 GB.
- **Labels:** Up to two cardiologists annotated each record with SCP-ECG statements (71 in total, covering diagnostic, form and rhythm categories). A technical expert validated the signals. Folds 9 and 10 had at least one human evaluation, so their label quality is particularly high. That makes them a natural test set.
- **Your targets:** The page doesn't list the individual statements, so I couldn't confirm AF, bundle branch block or AV block labels from it. From memory, `scp_statements.csv` includes AFIB, CLBBB, CRBBB and 1AVB/2AVB/3AVB. Check that file first.
- **Download:** `physionet download ptb-xl --version 1.0.3`, or `aws s3 sync --no-sign-request s3://physionet-open/ptb-xl/1.0.3/ DEST`.

**2. Chapman-Shaoxing + Ningbo ("ecg-arrhythmia" v1.0.0; best for AF volume)**
- **Size:** 45,152 twelve-lead ECGs at 500 Hz, about 5.1 GB uncompressed (2.3 GB ZIP). A search result (not the PhysioNet page) says the Chapman-Shaoxing cohort alone has 3,889 AF subjects.
- **Labels:** A licensed physician labeled each recording, a second physician validated, and a senior physician settled disagreements. They are stored as SNOMED-CT codes in the `.hea` headers.
- **Download:** `physionet download ecg-arrhythmia --version 1.0.0`, or the `aws s3 sync --no-sign-request` command with `s3://physionet-open/ecg-arrhythmia/1.0.0/`.
- **Caveat:** The Scientific Data paper describes the first 10,646 patients as 10-second, 12-lead recordings. I didn't confirm the same for the Ningbo portion.

**3. PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021 training set (one SNOMED-coded bundle)**
- **Size:** More than 88,000 twelve-lead training ECGs, 12.6 GB. It includes CPSC 2018 and CPSC-Extra, Georgia, Chapman-Shaoxing/Ningbo, PTB/PTB-XL and INCART.
- **Why use it:** Several institutions in one uniform format with SNOMED-CT labels, which is useful for testing generalization across sites.
- **Download:** `physionet download challenge-2021 --version 1.0.3`.
- **Caveat:** The page says label quality varies by source, and some labels are human-overread machine labels. Use PTB-XL or ecg-arrhythmia if you need cardiologist-confirmed labels.

## Things to watch
- **Overlap:** The Challenge bundle already contains PTB-XL and Chapman/Ningbo. Don't combine it with those two datasets, or you'll get duplicates and leakage between train and test.
- **Recording length:** Not every Challenge source is a clean 10-second, 12-lead recording. For example, INCART is cut from Holter recordings. I'd drop INCART or check durations.
- **Label mapping:** PTB-XL uses SCP codes and the other two use SNOMED-CT, so you'll need a mapping table to harmonize them.
- **Version number:** The PTB-XL page gives two counts (21,799 and 21,801). I used 21,799, which the page and later papers mainly cite.

My suggestion is to start with PTB-XL, using folds 9 and 10 as your cleanly labeled test set. Then add ecg-arrhythmia for more AF and conduction cases and external validation.

Sources:
- [PTB-XL v1.0.3 (PhysioNet)](https://physionet.org/content/ptb-xl/1.0.3/)
- [PTB-XL paper (Scientific Data)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-020-0495-6)
- [ecg-arrhythmia v1.0.0 (PhysioNet)](https://physionet.org/content/ecg-arrhythmia/1.0.0/)
- [Chapman-Shaoxing paper (Scientific Data)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-020-0386-x)
- [PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021 v1.0.3](https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2021/1.0.3/)
- [Challenge 2021 site](https://moody-challenge.physionet.org/2021/)
